title: Al-Wadud, the Loving
tomorrow: should praise for God be loud, or under your breath?

cards: Chemistry flashcards on the kitchen counter at six in the morning, in her dad's handwriting. Yusuf has never once said I love you out loud to Amira.
But there they are, a stack of them, for the chem test she mentioned once, days away. Love turns up in odd places. So does today's Name.
In Surah Al-Buruj: "And He is the Forgiving, the Loving." Here's the puzzle. Why put the Loving right beside the Forgiving?
Wouldn't love go with the people who got everything right?

teach.b: Look for the same pairing somewhere else, and you find it in Surah Hud. The prophet Shu'ayb tells his people: ask your Lord for pardon, then turn back to Him, for my Lord is Merciful and Loving. There's the answer.

In both places, love isn't a prize handed out at the end of a clean record. It's what's waiting on the other side of the turn back. Al-Wadud, the Loving, loves the one who comes back, not only the one who never left.
Here's the detail worth telling a friend tonight. Scholars of the Names notice that wadud can be read two ways in Arabic: the one who loves, and the one who is loved. Al-Ghazali took it further.
Al-Wadud, he wrote, is the one who wants good for all, and shows it in what He does. Love you can see. Not a feeling kept in a drawer, but love with hands.
A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari shows where that love goes.
When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril: I love this one, so love them.

teach.h: THE ONE WHO LOVES, AND IS LOVED.
teach.b: Jibril loves them, and calls it out to the heavens, and acceptance is placed for them on the earth.
Which explains flashcards at six in the morning. Some people say it. Some people write out a stack of formulas in the dark.

how: Muslims call on Allah as al-Wadud in du'a, and 85:14, 'the Forgiving, the Loving', is recited as a reminder that turning back is met with love.

o: the one who arranges every marriage
the one who loves only the righteous
the Loving, whose love shows in deeds

games.q: where the love shows — tap the pairs.
p: told to love the one Allah loves

s: in the Qur'an, 'the Loving' is paired with 'the Forgiving'
"And He is the Forgiving, the Loving" (85:14, Pickthall).
Al-Wadud loves only people with a clean record
Shu'ayb names his Lord Loving right after 'ask pardon, then turn back' (11:90).
wadud can be read as the one who loves and the one who is loved
scholars of the Names note both readings.

games.q: you snapped at your mom yesterday and haven't apologized. you're sure she's still upset, so you're avoiding her. what does today's puzzle suggest?
o: turn back first; love waits on the other side of the turn.
wait until you've earned it back by being perfect for a week.
skip the apology; love means she'll get over it anyway.
games.why: in 11:90 and 85:14, love sits right beside forgiveness: it's met in the turning back, not earned before it.

practice: Choose one deed of love you can do in the next minute, without announcing it: refill someone's water bottle, plug in a parent's phone, send the photo your grandmother asked for last week.
Do it now if you can, or decide exactly when. Love with hands doesn't need an audience. Then come back and sit.

wordCard.voice: Al-Wadud. The Loving, whose love shows in what He does, and waits on the other side of the turn back. Name forty-seven.

orig.note: Arabic: the Loving. scholars read it two ways: the one who loves, and the one who is loved.

carryVoice: Hold onto this one: loving, with hands, and with a door that stays open. Forty-seven names in.
